title: The death of the West's de minimis exemptions
snippet: Read in full. Macro logistics view: the US $800 exemption suspended and upheld by the Court of International Trade on 13 August 2026, the EU EUR 150 threshold scrapped on 1 July 2026 and replaced by a temporary EUR 3-per-item duty, the UK phasing out GBP 135 relief by October 2028. States the EU EUR 3 figure but publishes no per-parcel or per-item cost table, no worked example, and no comparison of what the same consignment pays in each market. Its analysis is about clearance workload and the shift to bulk freight.

title: The end of de minimis: New US entry processes, EU duties
snippet: Recorded honestly: my own fetch of this page returned navigation furniture with a truncated body, so I could not read it. The gate's dynamic fetch retrieved it and measured 5,342 words with 16 figures and per-unit arithmetic, and no cost table. So this is the strongest competitor in the set on figure density, and the reason the cross-source claim failed. It is also the reason the custom-calculation claim is the accurate one: it discusses the charges but publishes no comparable numeric cost table.

title: European Union moves to revoke duty-free status for parcel imports
snippet: Trade press on the EU decision itself. Directional coverage of the policy change; not an importer-level cost comparison and no per-item arithmetic.

title: EU Plans to End De Minimis Rule, Adding New Fees to Small Parcels
snippet: Trade press on the EU handling fee. Reports the fee and the policy direction; no cross-border comparison and no worked consignment.

title: What Is De Minimis? The End of Duty-Free Parcels in 2026
snippet: Explainer aimed at e-commerce sellers. Defines the exemption and summarises the changes by market. Definitional rather than arithmetical — no per-item charges computed for a named consignment.

title: De Minimis Threshold by Country 2026: Limits & Changes
snippet: Reference table of thresholds by country. Gives the thresholds, which both of our articles already publish, and does not compute what a consignment pays on either side.
